q: For positive numbers a and b, which of the following always holds?
x: The arithmetic mean of two positive numbers is at least the geometric mean: (a + b)/2 ≥ √(ab), since (√a − √b)² ≥ 0. a + b ≥ 2ab fails for a = b = 2 (4 < 8), and a² + b² < 2ab contradicts (a − b)² ≥ 0.

q: In an arithmetic sequence, a₁ = 3 and the common difference is d = 4. What is the value of a₁₀?
x: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d, so a₁₀ = 3 + 9 × 4 = 39. Using 10d instead of 9d gives 43, and leaving out a₁ gives 36.

q: In a geometric sequence, a₁ = 2 and the common ratio is q = 3. What is the value of a₅?
x: aₙ = a₁qⁿ⁻¹, so a₅ = 2 × 3⁴ = 2 × 81 = 162. Using 3⁵ instead of 3⁴ gives 486, and 54 is a₄.

q: A sequence satisfies a₁ = 1 and aₙ₊₁ = aₙ + 2n for n ≥ 1. What is the value of a₁₀?
x: Adding the differences, a₁₀ = 1 + 2(1 + 2 + … + 9) = 1 + 2 × 45 = 91 (generally aₙ = n² − n + 1). Adding up to 2 × 10 instead of 2 × 9 gives 111, and 73 is a₉.

q: The positive number G makes 4, G, 9 a geometric sequence. What is G?
x: G² = 4 × 9 = 36 and G > 0, so G = 6. The value 6.5 is the arithmetic mean of 4 and 9, which would make an arithmetic sequence instead.

q: What is the sum of the first 20 positive odd numbers, 1 + 3 + 5 + … + 39?
x: This is arithmetic with a₁ = 1, a₂₀ = 39, so S₂₀ = 20(1 + 39)/2 = 400 (in general the first n odd numbers add to n²). 420 is the sum of the first 20 even numbers, and 210 is 1 + 2 + … + 20.

q: Which of the following is a geometric sequence?
x: In 5, −10, 20, −40, … each term is the previous one multiplied by −2, so the ratio is constant. 3, 6, 9, 12 has a constant difference (arithmetic), not a constant ratio; 1, 2, 4, 7, 11 and the squares have neither.
1/((2k − 1)(2k + 1)) = ½[1/(2k − 1) − 1/(2k + 1)], so the sum telescopes to ½(1 − 1/21) = ½ × 20/21 = 10/21. Forgetting the factor ½ gives 20/21.

q: In an arithmetic sequence, a₃ = 7 and a₇ = 19. What is the value of a₁₀?
x: a₇ − a₃ = 4d = 12, so d = 3 and a₁₀ = a₇ + 3d = 19 + 9 = 28. Dividing 12 by 3 instead of 4 gives d = 4 and the wrong value 31.

q: A geometric sequence has first term 3 and common ratio 2. What is the sum of its first 6 terms?
x: S₆ = a₁(q⁶ − 1)/(q − 1) = 3(64 − 1)/1 = 189. 93 is S₅ and 381 is S₇; 192 = 3 × 2⁶ forgets the − 1.
Rationalising, 1/(√k + √(k + 1)) = √(k + 1) − √k, so the sum telescopes to √25 − √1 = 5 − 1 = 4. Forgetting the leftover −√1 gives 5.

q: A sequence has general term aₙ = n² − 3n. What is the value of a₅?
x: a₅ = 5² − 3 × 5 = 25 − 15 = 10. The value 4 is a₄, and −10 comes from computing 15 − 25 the wrong way round.

q: What is the sum to infinity of the geometric series 12 + 6 + 3 + 3/2 + …?
x: a₁ = 12 and q = 1/2, so S = a₁/(1 − q) = 12/(1/2) = 24. Using 1 + q in the denominator gives 8, and 21 is only the sum of the first three terms.

q: A sequence has general term aₙ = n + 2ⁿ. What is the sum of its first 5 terms?
A sequence is defined by a₁ = 2 and aₙ₊₁ = 2aₙ − 1 for n ≥ 1. What is the value of a₅?
x: a₂ = 3, a₃ = 5, a₄ = 9, a₅ = 17 (in fact aₙ = 2ⁿ⁻¹ + 1). Stopping one step early gives 9, and one step too far gives 33.

q: In a geometric sequence with all terms positive, a₂ · a₈ = 36. What is the value of a₅?
x: Since 2 + 8 = 5 + 5, a₂a₈ = a₅², so a₅² = 36 and a₅ = 6 (positive). Halving 36 (as if it were an arithmetic mean) gives the wrong value 18.

q: The sequence {aₙ} has aₙ = n · 2ⁿ⁻¹. Which expression equals the sum of its first n terms, Sₙ?
x: Sₙ = 1 + 2·2 + 3·2² + … + n·2ⁿ⁻¹ and 2Sₙ = 1·2 + 2·2² + … + n·2ⁿ. Subtracting, −Sₙ = (1 + 2 + … + 2ⁿ⁻¹) − n·2ⁿ = 2ⁿ − 1 − n·2ⁿ, so Sₙ = (n − 1)2ⁿ + 1. Check: S₂ = 1 + 4 = 5 = 1 × 4 + 1, while n·2ⁿ − 1 gives 7.

q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 5 and common difference 3. What is the sum of its first 12 terms?
x: a₁₂ = 5 + 11 × 3 = 38, so S₁₂ = 12(5 + 38)/2 = 6 × 43 = 258. Taking a₁₂ = 5 + 12 × 3 = 41 gives 276, and forgetting to halve gives 516.

q: A geometric sequence has first term 5 and common ratio −1/2. Which statement is true?
o: The terms alternate in sign and the sum to infinity is 10/3
The terms decrease and the sum to infinity is 10
The terms alternate in sign and the sum to infinity is 10
The sum to infinity does not exist
x: A negative ratio makes the signs alternate, and since |q| = 1/2 < 1 the sum to infinity is 5/(1 − (−1/2)) = 5/(3/2) = 10/3. The value 10 comes from using 1 − 1/2 and ignoring the sign of q.

q: What is the sum of the infinite series 1/(1 × 3) + 1/(2 × 4) + 1/(3 × 5) + … + 1/(n(n + 2)) + …?
x: 1/(n(n + 2)) = ½[1/n − 1/(n + 2)]. The partial sum telescopes to ½[1 + 1/2 − 1/(n + 1) − 1/(n + 2)], which tends to ½ × 3/2 = 3/4. Keeping only the 1 and forgetting the surviving 1/2 gives 1/2.

q: Three numbers are inserted between 4 and 24 so that the five numbers form an arithmetic sequence. What is the common difference?
x: The five terms have four gaps, so 4d = 24 − 4 = 20 and d = 5 (the sequence is 4, 9, 14, 19, 24). Dividing by 3, the number of inserted terms, gives the wrong value 20/3.

q: In a geometric sequence of real numbers, a₂ = 6 and a₅ = 162. What is a₁?
x: a₅/a₂ = q³ = 27, so q = 3 and a₁ = a₂/q = 6/3 = 2. The value 18 multiplies by q instead of dividing, and 3 is the ratio, not the first term.

q: Here lg denotes the logarithm to base 10. What is the value of lg(2/1) + lg(3/2) + lg(4/3) + … + lg(100/99)?
x: lg((k + 1)/k) = lg(k + 1) − lg k, so the sum telescopes to lg 100 − lg 1 = 2. Stopping the telescoping at lg 99 forgets that the last term contributes lg 100.

q: In an arithmetic sequence {aₙ}, a₃ + a₉ = 20. What is the sum of the first 11 terms, S₁₁?
x: Since 3 + 9 = 1 + 11, a₁ + a₁₁ = a₃ + a₉ = 20, so S₁₁ = 11 × 20/2 = 110. Forgetting to divide by 2 gives 220.

q: A geometric sequence with positive common ratio has S₃ = 7 and S₆ = 63, where Sₙ is the sum of the first n terms. What is S₉?
x: S₆/S₃ = 1 + q³ = 9, so q³ = 8, q = 2, and a₁(1 + 2 + 4) = 7 gives a₁ = 1. Then S₉ = 2⁹ − 1 = 511. Equivalently S₃, S₆ − S₃, S₉ − S₆ = 7, 56, 448. Multiplying 63 by 9 again (567) wrongly treats the sums themselves as geometric.

q: What is the value of 1 × 2 + 2 × 3 + 3 × 4 + … + 10 × 11?
x: k(k + 1) = k² + k, so the sum is (1² + … + 10²) + (1 + … + 10) = 385 + 55 = 440; equivalently n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3 = 10 × 11 × 12/3 = 440. The value 385 is only the sum of the squares, and 572 goes up to 11 × 12.

q: The sum of the first n terms of a sequence {aₙ} is Sₙ = n² + n + 1. Which statement about its general term is correct?
x: a₁ = S₁ = 3. For n ≥ 2, aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = (n² + n + 1) − ((n − 1)² + (n − 1) + 1) = 2n. Since 2 × 1 = 2 ≠ 3, the formula 2n does not hold for n = 1, so 'aₙ = 2n for all n' is wrong.

q: Two numbers are inserted between 3 and 81 so that the four numbers form a geometric sequence. What is the sum of the two inserted numbers?
x: 81 = 3q³ gives q³ = 27, q = 3, so the inserted numbers are 9 and 27, with sum 36. Inserting numbers to make an arithmetic sequence instead (29 and 55) gives 84.

q: A sequence satisfies a₁ = 2 and aₙ₊₁ − aₙ = 3ⁿ for n ≥ 1. What is its general term?
x: Adding the differences, aₙ = 2 + (3 + 3² + … + 3ⁿ⁻¹) = 2 + (3ⁿ − 3)/2 = (3ⁿ + 1)/2 (check: a₂ = 5, a₃ = 14). The formula 3ⁿ⁻¹ + 1 fits a₁ = 2 but gives a₂ = 4 instead of 5.

q: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 25 and common difference −3. For which value of n is the sum of the first n terms, Sₙ, the largest?
x: aₙ = 25 − 3(n − 1) = 28 − 3n, so a₉ = 1 > 0 and a₁₀ = −2 < 0. Sₙ grows while the added terms are positive, so it is largest at n = 9 (S₉ = 117). At n = 10 a negative term has already been added.

q: A ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. After each bounce it rises to half the height from which it last fell. In theory it bounces forever. What is the total vertical distance it travels?
x: Down 10 m, then each rise of 5, 2.5, … m is followed by an equal fall: total = 10 + 2(5 + 2.5 + …) = 10 + 2 × 5/(1 − ½) = 10 + 20 = 30 m. 20 m counts each bounce only once (10/(1 − ½)).
1/(k(k + 1)) = 1/k − 1/(k + 1), so the sum telescopes to 1 − 1/(n + 1) = n/(n + 1). Setting n/(n + 1) = 9/10 gives n = 9. Choosing 10 matches the denominator n + 1, not n.

q: A lecture hall has 15 rows of seats. The first row has 20 seats and each row after it has 2 more seats than the row in front. How many seats are there in total?
x: The last row has 20 + 14 × 2 = 48 seats, so the total is 15(20 + 48)/2 = 510. Taking the last row as 20 + 15 × 2 = 50 gives 525, and forgetting to halve gives 1020.

q: A geometric sequence has a₁ = 1 and common ratio 2. What is the smallest n for which the sum of the first n terms exceeds 1000?
x: Sₙ = 2ⁿ − 1, and 2⁹ − 1 = 511 < 1000 while 2¹⁰ − 1 = 1023 > 1000, so n = 10. Choosing 9 checks the term 2⁹ = 512 or the sum 511, neither of which is above 1000.

q: A sequence has general term aₙ = (2n − 1) + (1/2)ⁿ. Which expression gives the sum of its first n terms?
x: Sum the two parts separately: 1 + 3 + … + (2n − 1) = n², and 1/2 + 1/4 + … + 1/2ⁿ = 1 − 1/2ⁿ. So Sₙ = n² + 1 − 1/2ⁿ. Check n = 2: S₂ = 3/2 + 13/4 = 19/4 = 4 + 1 − 1/4, whereas n² + 1/2ⁿ gives 17/4.

q: How many terms of the A.P. 5, 9, 13, … must be added to give a sum of 275?
Ali saves Rs. 500 in the first month and Rs. 100 more each month than in the month before. How much does he save in total in the first 12 months?
x: The savings form an A.P. with a = 500, d = 100, n = 12: S₁₂ = (12/2)[2(500) + 11(100)] = 6 × 2100 = 12,600. Using 12d instead of 11d gives 13,200, and Rs. 1,600 is only the 12th month's saving.

q: How many integers between 100 and 500 are divisible by 7?
x: The multiples run 105, 112, …, 497, an A.P. with d = 7. From 497 = 105 + (n − 1)7, n − 1 = 56 and n = 57. Forgetting to add 1 gives 56.

q: a, b and c are in A.P. Which of these is also an A.P.?
o: b + c, c + a, a + b
x: The differences are (c + a) − (b + c) = a − b and (a + b) − (c + a) = b − c, and a − b = b − c because b − a = c − b. Test with 1, 2, 3: 5, 4, 3 is an A.P., but 1, 4, 9 is not; 2ᵃ, 2ᵇ, 2ᶜ is a G.P. and 1/a, 1/b, 1/c is an H.P.

q: In an A.P. the pth term is q and the qth term is p, where p ≠ q. What is the (p + q)th term?
x: a + (p − 1)d = q and a + (q − 1)d = p; subtracting gives (p − q)d = q − p, so d = −1 and a = p + q − 1. Then the (p + q)th term is a + (p + q − 1)(−1) = 0. Check: 5, 4, 3, 2, … has 2nd term 4 and 4th term 2, and its 6th term is 0.

q: Four arithmetic means are inserted between 3 and 23. What is the sum of the four means?
x: The six numbers form an A.P. with d = (23 − 3)/5 = 4: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23. The means sum to 7 + 11 + 15 + 19 = 52, which is 4 × (3 + 23)/2. 78 is the sum of all six numbers.

q: Three numbers in A.P. have sum 15 and product 80. What is the largest of them?
x: Write them as a − d, a, a + d. Then 3a = 15 gives a = 5, and 5(25 − d²) = 80 gives d² = 9, so the numbers are 2, 5, 8. Check: 2 × 5 × 8 = 80. The largest is 8 whichever sign d has.

q: Which fraction equals the recurring decimal 0.272727… ?
Three positive geometric means are inserted between 2 and 32. What is the product of the three means?
x: 2r⁴ = 32 gives r = 2, so the means are 4, 8, 16 with product 512 = 8³ (the middle mean is √(2 × 32) = 8). 28 is their sum, and 8 is only the middle mean.

q: For which values of x does the infinite series 1 + (x − 1) + (x − 1)² + … have a finite sum?
x: A geometric series converges exactly when its common ratio r = x − 1 satisfies |r| < 1, i.e. −1 < x − 1 < 1, so 0 < x < 2. The endpoints give r = ±1, where the series does not converge; −1 < x < 1 puts the condition on x instead of on x − 1.

q: An infinite G.P. has sum 8, and the sum of the squares of its terms is 32. What is its first term?
Bilal buys a car for Rs. 2,000,000. Its value falls by 20% of its value at the start of each year. What is its value after 3 years?
x: The values form a G.P. with ratio 0.8: 2,000,000 × 0.8³ = 2,000,000 × 0.512 = 1,024,000. Subtracting 20% of the original price each year (a fall of 3 × 400,000) gives 1,200,000, and 1,280,000 is the value after 2 years.

q: Which term of the G.P. 3, 6, 12, … is 384?
x: aₙ = 3 × 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 384 gives 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 128 = 2⁷, so n − 1 = 7 and n = 8. Taking n = 7 forgets the −1 in the exponent; 128 is the value of 2ⁿ⁻¹, not n.

q: Three numbers in G.P. have sum 13 and product 27, and the common ratio is greater than 1. What is the third number?
x: Write them as 3/r, 3, 3r, since the product (3/r)(3)(3r) = 27 gives the middle term 3. Then 3/r + 3 + 3r = 13 gives 3r² − 10r + 3 = 0, so r = 3 (r > 1) and the numbers are 1, 3, 9. Check: 1 + 3 + 9 = 13.

q: What is the harmonic mean of 3 and 6?
x: H = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 18/9 = 4. 9/2 is the arithmetic mean and 3√2 the geometric mean; 1/4 is the mean of the reciprocals, before taking the reciprocal again.

q: What is the 10th term of the H.P. 1/2, 1/5, 1/8, … ?
x: The reciprocals 2, 5, 8, … form an A.P. with d = 3, whose 10th term is 2 + 9 × 3 = 29. So the 10th term of the H.P. is 1/29. Using 10d gives 1/32; forgetting to take the reciprocal back gives 29.

q: Which of these sequences is a harmonic progression?
x: The reciprocals of 6, 3, 2, 3/2 are 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6, an A.P. with difference 1/6, so it is an H.P. The reciprocals 1, 2, 4, 8 form a G.P.; 2, 4, 6, 8 is itself an A.P.; and 1, 4, 9, 16 is not an A.P.

q: The 3rd term of an H.P. is 1/5 and its 7th term is 1/13. What is its 12th term?
x: The reciprocals form an A.P. with a + 2d = 5 and a + 6d = 13, so d = 2 and a = 1. Its 12th term is 1 + 11 × 2 = 23, so the H.P. term is 1/23. Using 12d gives 1/25.

q: The arithmetic mean of two positive numbers is 5 and their geometric mean is 4. What is their harmonic mean?
x: For two positive numbers G² = AH, so H = G²/A = 16/5. Check: the numbers are 2 and 8 (sum 10, product 16), and 2 × 16/10 = 16/5. 20 is A × G, not the HM.

q: Two positive numbers have arithmetic mean 10 and harmonic mean 6.4. What is the larger number?
x: G² = AH = 10 × 6.4 = 64, so the product is 64 and the sum is 20. The numbers are the roots of t² − 20t + 64 = 0, namely 4 and 16. Check: 2 × 64/20 = 6.4.

q: Two harmonic means are inserted between 1/3 and 1/12. What are they?
x: The reciprocals 3, _, _, 12 form an A.P. with d = (12 − 3)/3 = 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. So the harmonic means are 1/6 and 1/9. 1/4 and 1/6 are the arithmetic means of 1/3 and 1/12.

q: a, b and c are distinct and in H.P. Which relation is true?
x: With b = 2ac/(a + c): a − b = a(a − c)/(a + c) and b − c = c(a − c)/(a + c), so the ratio is a/c. Check with 1, 1/2, 1/3: (1/2)/(1/6) = 3 = a/c. The ratio 1 is the A.P. condition.

q: For positive unequal numbers a and b, the expression (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) equals their harmonic mean for which value of n?
x: With n = −1 the expression is (1 + 1)/(1/a + 1/b) = 2ab/(a + b), the harmonic mean. n = 0 gives (a + b)/2, the arithmetic mean, and n = −1/2 gives √(ab), the geometric mean.

q: Hamza drives from Lahore to Faisalabad at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 40 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole trip?
x: Equal distances make the average speed the harmonic mean: 2 × 60 × 40/(60 + 40) = 48 km/h. Check with 120 km each way: 2 h + 3 h = 5 h for 240 km. 50 km/h is the arithmetic mean, which assumes equal times.

q: The first two terms of an H.P. are 2 and 3. What is its third term?
x: The reciprocals 1/2, 1/3 form an A.P. with d = −1/6, so the third reciprocal is 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6 and the third term is 6. Continuing 2, 3 as an A.P. gives 4, and as a G.P. gives 9/2; 12/5 is the HM of 2 and 3.

q: Harmonic means are inserted between 1 and 1/21 so that the reciprocals of all the terms form an A.P. with common difference 4. How many means are inserted?
x: The reciprocals run 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21: (21 − 1)/4 = 5 steps, so there are 5 + 1 = 6 terms in all and 4 means (1/5, 1/9, 1/13, 1/17). 5 counts the steps rather than the means.

q: Three nonzero numbers a, b, c are in A.P. and also in H.P. Which must be true?
x: From the A.P., b = (a + c)/2; from the H.P., b = 2ac/(a + c). Equating gives (a + c)² = 4ac, i.e. (a − c)² = 0, so a = c and then b = a. They are then also in G.P., but only trivially.

q: a, b and c are nonzero and in A.P. with nonzero common difference. Which of these sequences is an H.P.?
x: Dividing bc, ca, ab by abc gives 1/a, 1/b, 1/c, so the reciprocals of bc, ca, ab are a/(abc), b/(abc), c/(abc), an A.P. Hence bc, ca, ab is an H.P. Test with 1, 2, 3: 6, 3, 2 has reciprocals 1/6, 2/6, 3/6. 2a, 2b, 2c and a + 1, b + 1, c + 1 are A.P.s.

q: For positive numbers a and b, what is the least value of (a + b)(1/a + 1/b)?
x: A ≥ H gives (a + b)/2 ≥ 2/(1/a + 1/b), so (a + b)(1/a + 1/b) ≥ 4, with equality at a = b (e.g. a = b = 1 gives 2 × 2 = 4). Equally, the product is 2 + a/b + b/a and a/b + b/a ≥ 2.

q: What is the value of 1² + 2² + 3² + … + 10²?
For which n is 1³ + 2³ + … + n³ = 1296?
x: Σk³ = [n(n + 1)/2]², so n(n + 1)/2 = √1296 = 36 and n(n + 1) = 72, n = 8. Check: 8 × 9/2 = 36. 36 is the value of n(n + 1)/2, not n.

q: What is the value of 11² + 12² + 13² + … + 20²?
x: Subtract the first ten squares from the first twenty: 20 × 21 × 41/6 − 385 = 2870 − 385 = 2485. Subtracting up to 11² instead of 10² gives 2870 − 506 = 2364; 2870 forgets to subtract at all, and 3255 adds instead of subtracting.

q: What is the sum of the infinite series 1 + 2/3 + 3/9 + 4/27 + … ?
x: S = Σ n xⁿ⁻¹ with x = 1/3. S − S/3 = 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + … = 3/2, so (2/3)S = 3/2 and S = 9/4 = 1/(1 − x)². 3/2 is only the geometric part, before dividing by 2/3.

q: What is the value of 1² + 3² + 5² + … + 19²?
x: Σ(2k − 1)² for k = 1 to 10 equals 4Σk² − 4Σk + 10 = 4(385) − 4(55) + 10 = 1330. Check: the squares of 1 to 20 sum to 2870, the even squares 4 × 385 = 1540, and 2870 − 1540 = 1330. Dropping the +10 gives 1320.

q: The nth term of a series is n² + 2n. Which expression is the sum of its first n terms?
x: Σ(k² + 2k) = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 + n(n + 1) = n(n + 1)(2n + 1 + 6)/6 = n(n + 1)(2n + 7)/6. Check n = 2: 3 + 8 = 11 and 2 × 3 × 11/6 = 11. Writing Σ2k as 2n gives the third expression.
